# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 6 (Bu-Vb Ss6)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Ss6  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 6  
**Title (English, from literature):** Building a hut inappropriately  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Kuṭikāra* ("Building a hut inappropriately") is the sixth training rule of the Saṅghādisesa category in the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. The rule regulates individual monastic dwellings, prescribing that whenever a bhikkhu constructs a hut by begging for materials, he must obtain formal approval from the Saṅgha regarding the building site, and the dwelling must not exceed specified maximum dimensions; breaching either of these stipulations incurs an offense entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*). The rule's canonical origin story incorporates the *Maṇikaṇṭha Jātaka*—found in slightly different form in the canonical Jātaka collection (Ja 253)—alongside an additional edifying tale aligned with the *Aṭṭhisenaka Jātaka* (Ja 403) and an apparent reference to Raṭṭhapāla of the *Raṭṭhapāla Sutta* (MN 82).

Full parallels are widely attested across all major early Vinaya traditions, with corresponding rules and analyses preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions of the Dharmaguptaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions, as well as the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra*.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
